advil.t: Ibuprofen is used to relieve pain, tenderness, swelling, and stiffness caused by osteoarthritis (arthritis caused by a breakdown of the lining of the joints) and rheumatoid arthritis (arthritis caused by swelling of the lining of the joints).

amitriptyline.t: Used to treat symptoms of depression.

benadryl.t: Diphenhydramine is used to treat allergy and cold symptoms: sneezing; runny nose; red, itchy, watery eyes; itching of the nose or throat.

buspar.t: Buspirone is used to treat anxiety.

ciprofloxacin.t: Used to treat or prevent certain infections caused by bacteria.

dicyclomine.t: Used to treat the symptoms of irritable bowel syndrome.

diphenhydramine.t: Used to treat allergy and cold symptoms: sneezing; runny nose; red, itchy, watery eyes; itching of the nose or throat.

dronabinol.t: Used to treat nausea and vomiting caused by chemotherapy in people who have already taken other medications to treat this type of nausea and vomiting without good results.

famotidine.t: Used to treat ulcers (sores on the lining of the stomach or small intestine); gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD, a condition in which backward flow of acid from the stomach causes heartburn and injury of the esophagus [tube that connects the mouth and stomach]); and conditions where the stomach produces too much acid, such as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (tumors in the pancreas or small intestine that cause increased production of stomach acid).

fluconazole.t: Used to treat fungal infections, including yeast infections of the vagina, mouth, throat, esophagus (tube leading from the mouth to the stomach), abdomen (area between the chest and waist), lungs, blood, and other organs.

folic acid.t: Used to treat or prevent folic acid deficiency.

granisetron.t: Used to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by cancer chemotherapy and radiation therapy.

ibuprofen.t: Used to relieve pain, tenderness, swelling, and stiffness caused by osteoarthritis (arthritis caused by a breakdown of the lining of the joints) and rheumatoid arthritis (arthritis caused by swelling of the lining of the joints).

lactulose.t: A synthetic sugar used to treat constipation.

leucovorin.t: Used to prevent harmful effects of methotrexate (a cancer chemotherapy medication) or to treat an overdose of methotrexate or similar medications.

levofloxacin.t: Used to treat certain infections caused by bacteria.

lorazepam.t: Used to relieve anxiety and treat insomnia.

mesna.t: Used to reduce the risk of hemorrhagic cystitis (a condition that causes inflammation of the bladder and can result in serious bleeding) in people who receive ifosfamide (a medication used for the treatment of cancer).

metoclopramide.t: Used to treat gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD; condition in which backward flow of acid from the stomach causes heartburn and injury of the esophagus) and gastroparesis (slow stomach emptying).

motrin.t: Ibuprofen is used to relieve pain, tenderness, swelling, and stiffness caused by osteoarthritis (arthritis caused by a breakdown of the lining of the joints) and rheumatoid arthritis (arthritis caused by swelling of the lining of the joints).

ondansetron.t: Used to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by cancer chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and surgery.

paroxetine.t: Used to treat depression, panic disorder (sudden, unexpected attacks of extreme fear and worry about these attacks), social anxiety disorder (extreme fear of interacting with others or performing in front of others that interferes with normal life), obsessive-compulsive disorder (bothersome thoughts that won't go away and the need to perform certain actions over and over), generalized anxiety disorder (GAD; excessive worrying that is difficult to control), and posttraumatic stress disorder (disturbing psychological symptoms that develop after a frightening experience).

pepcid.t: Famotidine is used to treat ulcers (sores on the lining of the stomach or small intestine); gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD, a condition in which backward flow of acid from the stomach causes heartburn and injury of the esophagus [tube that connects the mouth and stomach]); and conditions where the stomach produces too much acid, such as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (tumors in the pancreas or small intestine that cause increased production of stomach acid).

promethazine.t: Used to relieve the symptoms of allergic reactions such as allergic rhinitis (runny nose and watery eyes caused by allergy to pollen, mold or dust), allergic conjunctivitis (red, watery eyes caused by allergies), allergic skin reactions, and allergic reactions to blood or plasma products.

scopolamine.t: Used to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by motion sickness or medications used during surgery.

sertraline.t: Used to treat depression, obsessive-compulsive disorder (bothersome thoughts that won't go away and the need to perform certain actions over and over), panic attacks (sudden, unexpected attacks of extreme fear and worry about these attacks), posttraumatic stress disorder (disturbing psychological symptoms that develop after a frightening experience), and social anxiety disorder (extreme fear of interacting with others or performing in front of others that interferes with normal life).

zofran.t: Ondansetron is used to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by cancer chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and surgery.
